extracted.intended_audience: Members of the public, stakeholders, and regulated entities who wish to submit comments on NHTSA's proposed SAFE Vehicles Rule III and Draft SEIS
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural guidance for submitting and handling public comments on NHTSA's proposed SAFE Vehicles Rule III and accompanying Draft Supplemental Environmental Impact Statement, including an announced extension of the comment period and the agency's reasons for denying additional hearings. Targets participation in this specific rulemaking docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment deadline / extension
rubrics_metrics.description: The comment period for the proposed rule (90 FR 56438) published December 5, 2025, is extended. Comments on the proposed rule and Draft SEIS must be received by February 4. Late-filed comments may be considered so far as possible without incurring additional expense or delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHTSA is extending the public comment period by 15 days to February 4, 2026—a total of 60 days—because the agency believes that this amount of time should be adequate for commenters to review fully and comment meaningfully on the proposed rule and on the Draft SEIS. The agency balanced the public interest in timely completion of the final rule with prior NHTSA CAFE comment periods and comment periods for other significant rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for submitting comments
rubrics_metrics.description: You may submit comments to the docket number identified in the heading of this document by any of the following methods: Federal eRulemaking Portal (http://www.regulations.gov), mail, hand delivery or courier, or fax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow online instructions at Regulations.gov. Mail to Docket Management Facility at U.S. Department of Transportation, 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, West Building Ground Floor, Room W12-140, Washington, DC 20590-0001. Hand delivery/courier to the same address between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET, Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays. Fax: 202-493-2251. All submissions must include the agency name and docket number. Note that all comments received will be posted without change to http://www.regulations.gov, including any personal information provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket access and reviewing background documents
rubrics_metrics.description: For access to the docket to read background documents or comments received, go to http://www.regulations.gov at any time or to 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, West Building Ground Floor, Room W12-140, Washington, DC between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, except Federal Holidays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telephone: 202-366-9826. The Federal Register site also links to supporting documents in the docket (e.g., non-copyrighted references, data files). Use the docket to locate supporting documents referenced by the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act / public posting of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 5 U.S.C. 553(c), DOT solicits comments from the public to better inform its decision-making process. DOT posts these comments, without edit, including any personal information the commenter provides, to www.regulations.gov, as described in the system of records notice (DOT/ALL-14 FDMS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To facilitate comment tracking and response, commenters are encouraged to provide their name or organization name; however, submission of names is optional. Whether or not commenters identify themselves, all timely comments will be fully considered. Because comments are posted without change, do not include information you do not want publicly displayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Business Information (CBI) submission procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If you wish to submit any information under a claim of confidentiality, you must submit your request directly to NHTSA's Office of the Chief Counsel. Requests for confidentiality are governed by 49 CFR part 512.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHTSA is treating electronic submission as an acceptable method for submitting CBI under part 512. Email Dan Rabinovitz in the Office of the Chief Counsel at Daniel.Rabinovitz@dot.gov or contact him for a secure file transfer link. Do not send a duplicate hardcopy of electronic CBI submissions to DOT headquarters. If you claim information constitutes CBI under 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(4) or is protected under 18 U.S.C. 1905, you must submit supporting information together with the materials that are the subject of the confidentiality request in accordance with part 512. Your request must include a cover letter setting forth the information specified in 49 CFR 512.8 and a certificate pursuant to § 512.4(b) and part 512, Appendix A. Also submit a copy from which you have deleted the claimed CBI to the Docket at the address provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (information collection) comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on the proposed information collection requirements should be submitted to the Office of Management and Budget at www.reginfo.gov/public/do/PRAMain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To find the information collection, select 'Currently under Review—Open for Public Comment' or use the search function on reginfo.gov. It is requested that comments sent to OMB also be sent to the NHTSA rulemaking docket identified in the heading of this document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency criteria and rationale for extending comment periods and denying additional hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesters asked for longer comment periods and additional public hearings, citing the time needed for careful analysis and review, technically complex changes from prior analyses, and the proposed rule's potential significance on the U.S. economy, consumers, human health, and the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After consideration, NHTSA extended the comment period by 15 days (total 60 days), finding that amount adequate. NHTSA denied requests for additional public hearings because: (1) the agency reserved two days for the virtual hearing and the number of requestors to testify only covered part of one day; (2) a virtual public hearing format allows flexibility for diverse comments from multiple locations; and (3) given ongoing opportunity for written comment, requesters have not demonstrated a need for additional in-person hearings. The agency balanced requesters' needs against timely completion of the final rule and past practice (citing prior NHTSA CAFE comment periods and other significant rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency review, redaction, and availability of submitted comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies review all submissions and may choose to redact, or withhold, certain submissions (or portions thereof). Submitted comments may not be available to be read until the agency has approved them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although DOT posts comments without edit to Regulations.gov, agencies retain authority to withhold or redact material as necessary; availability on Regulations.gov may be delayed pending agency approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacts for further information
rubrics_metrics.description: For technical and policy issues, contact Joseph Bayer, CAFE Program Division Chief, Office of Rulemaking, NHTSA. For legal issues, contact Hannah Fish, NHTSA Office of the Chief Counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email for both contacts: CAFE_Mbox@dot.gov. Addresses provided: 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, Washington, DC 20590. Use these contacts for clarification about the proposed rule, Draft SEIS, or comment submission procedures.
